connectionsSaturated.title: Connections {{usedPct}} used ({{used}} of {{available}})
connectionsSaturated.fix: See who holds connections in Sessions grouped by application; use a pooler or smaller application pools.

idleInTransaction.title: Idle in transaction for {{maxS}}
idleInTransaction.fix: Such transactions hold locks and the xmin horizon: fix the missing COMMIT in the application, set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.

longQuery.title: A query has been running for {{maxS}}
longQuery.fix: Check its plan and locks; cancel it if it blocks others.

longTransaction.title: A transaction has been open for {{maxS}}
longTransaction.fix: Long transactions hold the xmin horizon and bloat tables: find the session and the application behind it.

xidAge.title: Transaction ID age is {{agePct}} of the wraparound limit
xidAge.fix: Find what holds vacuum (xmin horizon) and let autovacuum freeze the oldest tables.

lockWait.title: Sessions waiting for locks: {{count}}, the longest {{maxS}}
lockWait.fix: Open Locks to find the root blocker.

walDirSize.title: pg_wal is {{walDirBytes}} with max_wal_size {{maxWalSizeBytes}}
walDirSize.fix: WAL is usually held by an inactive replication slot or failing archiving: check Replication slots.

deadlocks.title: Deadlocks in the interval: {{count}}
deadlocks.fix: Details are only in the server log; make the application take locks in one order.

lockShare.title: Lock waits take {{sharePct}} of active time
lockShare.fix: Open Locks to find who blocks.

rootBlocker.title: Session {{pid}} blocks sessions: {{count}}, the longest wait {{maxS}}
rootBlocker.fix: Look at its transaction; cancelling or ending it releases the chain.

ddlQueue.title: DDL on {{relation}} is queued and blocks sessions: {{count}}
ddlQueue.fix: Cancel the DDL to release the queue, or the query it waits for; run migrations with lock_timeout.

xminHorizon.title: The xmin horizon is held by {{kindLabel}} {{name}} ({{xminAge}} transactions)
xminHorizon.fix: Vacuum cannot clean rows newer than the horizon: end the transaction, drop or fix the slot, or roll back the prepared transaction.

replicaLag.title: Replica lag: {{lag}}
replicaLag.fix: Check the replica's load, network and replay conflicts in Replicas.

replicaNotStreaming.title: Replicas not streaming: {{count}} (state {{state}})
replicaNotStreaming.fix: A replica in catchup or backup is not a failover candidate yet.

replicaReplyStale.title: Replicas silent for {{maxS}}: {{count}}
replicaReplyStale.fix: The replica stopped confirming WAL: check its network and wal_receiver_status_interval.

syncStandbyMissing.title: synchronous_standby_names is set but no synchronous replica is connected
syncStandbyMissing.fix: Commits wait for a synchronous replica: bring one back or change synchronous_standby_names.

walReceiverDown.title: The WAL receiver is not streaming
walReceiverDown.fix: The replica is not receiving WAL from its upstream: check primary_conninfo, the slot and the network.

replayPaused.title: WAL replay is paused
replayPaused.fix: Resume it with pg_wal_replay_resume() if the pause is not intentional.

recoveryConflicts.title: New recovery conflicts: {{count}}
recoveryConflicts.fix: Queries on the replica are cancelled to apply WAL: consider hot_standby_feedback or max_standby_streaming_delay.

recoveryConflictsTotal.title: Recovery conflicts since the statistics reset: {{count}}
recoveryConflictsTotal.fix: No new conflicts now; watch the counter.

slotRetainsWal.title: Inactive slot {{name}} retains {{retainedBytes}} of WAL
slotRetainsWal.fix: If its consumer is gone, drop the slot; otherwise bring the consumer back; set max_slot_wal_keep_size.

slotLost.title: Slot {{name}} lost the WAL it needs
slotLost.fix: The consumer cannot continue: drop the slot and resynchronize the consumer.

subscriptionErrors.title: New subscription errors: {{count}}
subscriptionErrors.fix: Details are in the subscriber's server log.

failoverCandidates.title: Failover candidates ready: {{count}}
failoverCandidates.fix: See the reasons per replica in Failover readiness.

clusterPaused.title: The cluster is paused: automatic failover is off
clusterPaused.fix: Resume the cluster when maintenance is over.

syncModeWithoutSync.title: synchronous_mode is on but there is no synchronous replica
syncModeWithoutSync.fix: Failover is impossible and with synchronous_mode_strict writes stop: bring a replica back to sync.

patroniTiming.title: ttl {{ttlS}} is less than loop_wait {{loopWaitS}} + 2 × retry_timeout {{retryTimeoutS}}
patroniTiming.fix: The leader key may expire during a DCS hiccup: raise ttl (patronictl edit-config).

healthPrimary.title: The leader address answers 200 on members: {{count}}
healthPrimary.fix: A load balancer would send writes to the wrong place or nowhere: check the topology.

healthUnhealthy.title: {{member}}: /health does not answer 200
healthUnhealthy.fix: PostgreSQL on the member is not running.

replicaOutOfPool.title: {{member}} is a replica but /replica does not answer 200
replicaOutOfPool.fix: The load balancer excludes it from reads: lag, the noloadbalance tag or a stopped replica.

cacheHitLow.title: Cache hit in the interval: {{hitPct}}
cacheHitLow.fix: Reads go to disk: check heavy queries and shared_buffers.

tempFiles.title: Temporary files in the interval: {{count}}
tempFiles.fix: Sorts and hashes spill to disk: look at work_mem for the heavy queries.

noIdleTimeout.title: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is off
noIdleTimeout.fix: Set it for the application role: {{command}}

hiddenQueries.title: Texts of sessions are hidden: {{count}}
hiddenQueries.fix: Grant pg_monitor to the diagnostics role.

lockCycle.title: Sessions waiting for each other: {{count}}
lockCycle.fix: The deadlock detector will resolve it within deadlock_timeout; details are in the server log.

connections.connstr: JDBC (jdbc:postgresql://h1,h2/db), URI (postgresql://…) or host=… port=…. A password in the string is saved to the secret store.
connections.kind: Server — one PostgreSQL. Host list — several servers, roles are detected automatically. Patroni cluster — REST API addresses, nodes are discovered automatically.
connections.target: Which node the catalog is read from by default — like targetServerType in JDBC.
connections.overrides: If Patroni returns addresses your computer cannot reach (pod IP, NAT), set a reachable host, port and API address for the member.
connections.sslMode: prefer — TLS if possible, no certificate check even with a CA file; require — TLS only, a CA file adds a certificate check; verify-ca — check the certificate; verify-full — also the host name.
connections.pgpass: If no password is set, ~/.pgpass is used, as in psql.
connections.environment: Marks the connection with a color. prod connections ask you to type the connection name before any change.
connections.readOnly: Blocks everything that changes data or the cluster. Recommended for prod.
connections.sshTarget: A host or an alias from ~/.ssh/config, not user@host: enter the user in the “SSH user” field. ProxyJump, the agent and hardware keys are honored. Port and user come from the config when empty.

import.target: Where new folders and connections go. Existing ones stay where they are.
import.updateExisting: Existing connections get the settings from the file and keep their place. Saved passwords are kept only if the connection settings (address, user, database, TLS, Patroni, SSH) do not change.

diag.idleTimeout: Ends sessions idle in a transaction longer than this. Set it per application role; 0 — off.
diag.pulse: A summary per node: connections, TPS, cache hits, WAL, long transactions and queries, lock waits, XID age and lag. A highlighted cell opens the tool that explains it.
diag.sessions: Sessions from pg_stat_activity: what they run, what they wait for and how long they hold a transaction. Presets and grouping show who uses the connections.
diag.idleTx: Sessions that opened a transaction and do nothing. They hold locks and the xmin horizon until the application ends the transaction.
diag.waits: While this tab is open, the sampler records once a second what active sessions wait for. Bar height is the average number of active sessions, color is the wait class.
diag.locks: Who blocks whom: a tree from the root blocker down to its victims. Queued DDL is doubly dangerous: it waits itself and holds up every later query on the table.
diag.horizon: The oldest transaction whose row versions are still needed: VACUUM cannot remove newer dead rows, so tables bloat. Held by long transactions, prepared transactions, slots and hot_standby_feedback.
diag.replication: On a primary: the replicas it sends WAL to and their lag in bytes and time. On a replica: WAL receive and replay, replay pause and recovery conflicts.
diag.slots: A slot keeps WAL on the server until its consumer reads it. An inactive or lagging slot accumulates WAL and can fill the disk.
diag.failover: Whether Patroni can fail over to a replica if the leader fails: a verdict and reasons for each candidate, next to the settings it depends on.
diag.health: Response codes of Patroni REST API endpoints per member, as a load balancer sees them. 200 means the node fits the endpoint, 503 means it does not.
diag.lastEnd: When the replica last reported a new WAL position to the primary. If nothing is written to the cluster, the position stays put and this time grows; that is normal.
